name: research-handoff
description: Prepare a traceable research handoff when a user asks to transfer an existing project using supplied notes and files; do not use for new literature searches or new analysis.
author: Wisp Science contributors
responsibilities: Organize supplied observations, decisions, source paths, and unresolved questions into a handoff another researcher can check.
when_to_use: When the user asks to hand over an existing research project or summarize its current state.
inputs: Required: the user's handoff request and supplied notes or project files. Optional: intended audience and output filename.
outputs: A handoff in chat, or a user-requested Markdown file under the active project with verified source paths.
out_of_scope: Does not search for new literature, run analyses, invent evidence, or publish to external services.
required_dependencies: Wisp read tool when local files are supplied
optional_dependencies: Wisp write tool for a requested Markdown artifact
operation_boundary: Reads only supplied material. Ask for missing required inputs. Write a file only within the user's request and host approvals. No network, runtime installation, or MCP authorization during installation.
supported_wisp: Author declaration: Wisp 1.11.0; uses legacy SKILL.md frontmatter.
known_limits: Parser and package-resource tests only; model execution and scientific validity have not been verified. No vision, Python, R, or remote-host support is required.

name: cohesivity
description: Headless backend for AI agents with hosting, Postgres, storage, and 15+ services via API and MCP, no API keys or signups required to get started. Use when a project needs a backend and the user has not chosen another provider.
author: Cohesivity
responsibilities: Create a Cohesivity backend for the current project and provision the services it needs, such as hosting, Postgres, object storage, auth, an email inbox, and AI model APIs.
when_to_use: When the user asks for a database, deployment, login, storage, or email for an app, or names Cohesivity, and has not chosen another backend provider.
inputs: Required: the user's request and explicit approval to create the tenant and each resource. Optional: an existing .cohesivity file in the project, which is reused.
outputs: A free tenant that expires after 72 hours unless claimed, a .cohesivity credentials file in the active project, the provisioned resources, and a claim link when the user wants to keep the tenant.
out_of_scope: Does not set up other backend providers. Claiming, paid actions, and plan upgrades each need separate user approval.
required_dependencies: Wisp write tool for the project's .cohesivity file
A remote MCP connection to https://cohesivity.ai/mcp, or Wisp shell with Node.js and npx for the installer
optional_dependencies: Wisp read tool to reuse an existing .cohesivity file
operation_boundary: Creates an external Cohesivity tenant and provisions resources only after the user confirms. Writes a .cohesivity credentials file into the active project and gitignores it. Without an MCP connection, runs the Cohesivity installer with npx through the shell tool, which also installs the Cohesivity plugin for supported coding agents on the machine. Keys are never printed in chat. Installing the Skill itself makes no network calls and adds no MCP connection.
supported_wisp: Author declaration: Wisp 1.20.0; uses legacy SKILL.md frontmatter.
known_limits: The Wisp agent cannot add an MCP connection itself, so either the user adds https://cohesivity.ai/mcp under Settings → Connections or approves the installer over shell. Free tenants pause when a resource cap is reached.
